svg.title: Explicit Modules, with a Go accent
svg.desc: A map of Mixology, a domain-first modular monolith. Three native surfaces call public Go operations. Seven bounded contexts own their capabilities. Public queries and owner-local events connect contexts; writes remain private. A command, prepared leaf reactions, and success audit share one SQLite transaction. Shared values, mechanisms, and explicit wiring support the modules; types and architecture tests enforce boundaries. Original infographic by Ryan Harris. Source baseline 0d5e64b0455f7a5c96d4afada64654a5fdbb9a2c.
svg.text: A domain-first modular monolith. Clear ownership. Little ceremony.
EACH ENTRYPOINT BUILDS THE APPLICATION THROUGH app.New

a.text: Typed facade calls · shared behavior · fresh operation context

svg.text: Districts show ownership. Their size and adjacency carry no dependency meaning.
Every capability keeps its vocabulary, rules, policy, persistence and native adapters close together.
Public contracts connect. Private writes stay owned.
Values, domain rules and Cedar policy
Package organization; models and policy support both reads and writes.

a.text: models / queries belong to their context
Each receiver writes its own state

svg.text: Public coupling is deliberate. Go internal + arch-lint protect the implementation boundary.
One domain command. One local commit.
ONE COMMAND + LEAF REACTIONS + ONE ACTIVITY SHARE A SQLITE TRANSACTION
For each event: prepare every receiver before applying any reaction. No cascading events.
On managed failure: roll back the changes, then audit the failed attempt separately.
Clean · Explicit · DDD · Fubu · Screaming Architecture → expressed through Go
